chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Musa al-Warraq, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abi Jarir al-Qummi, who said:
I asked al-ʿAbd عليه السلام about the nuṭfah, what diyah is due for it, and what is due for the ʿalaqah, and what is due for the formed muḍghah, and that which becomes established in the wombs.

He said: 'Indeed, it is created in its mother's womb, one creation after another: it is a nuṭfah for forty days, then it becomes an ʿalaqah for forty days, then a muḍghah for forty days. So for the nuṭfah there are forty dinars, for the ʿalaqah sixty dinars, for the muḍghah eighty dinars, and when the bones are clothed with flesh, then for it there are one hundred dinars. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:'
“Then We produced him as another creation; so blessed is Allah, the best of creators.”
'So if it is male, then for it is the diyah, and if it is female, then for her is her diyah.'

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: the prescribed blood-money compensation due in law
key_terms.النُّطْفَةِ: the seminal drop; the earliest stage of embryonic development
key_terms.الْأَرْحَامِ: the wombs, where fetal development takes place
key_terms.الْعَلَقَةِ: the clinging clot-like stage of embryonic development
key_terms.الْعِظَامُ: the bones, referring to a later stage of bodily formation
key_terms.الْمُضْغَةِ: the chewed-like lump stage of embryonic development
key_terms.خَلْقًا آخَرَ: another creation; indicating a further stage of development
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a dinar; the monetary unit used here to quantify diyah

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due for the different stages of fetal development in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the diyah amounts for different stages of fetal development, beginning from the nuṭfah and increasing through the stages of ʿalaqah, muḍghah, and the stage when the bones are clothed with flesh. It also cites a Qur'anic phrase to describe the progression of creation in the womb and concludes by distinguishing the applicable diyah according to whether the fetus is male or female.
